C# `ContentDecompositor` (ns `AiProxy.Core.Content`, `sealed`, implements `IDecompositor`). Splits payload by structure; unstructured text stays whole.

**Decompose(string content, string requestId)** → `Decomposition(requestId, content, template, parts)`. Each span becomes `ContentPart(requestId, chunkId, type, text)` (chunkId 1-based) and a placeholder `{<short>_<chunkId>}` in the template. Null args throw `ArgumentNullException`.

**ShortName**: Prose=prose, Log=log, Json=json, Xml=xml, Toml=toml, Markdown=markdown, SourceCode=code, DirectoryListing=listing, ShellTranscript=shell, other=unknown.

**FindParts** (line by line; `Span(Start, Length, Type, Structural)`):
1. Line trimmed starts with ``` or ~~~ → `FindFenceEnd` (closing line whose trimmed text is only that marker char; returns end or -1). If found → structural SourceCode span.
2. If `failedAttempts < 32`:
   - Trimmed starts `{` or `[` → `FindJsonEnd` (brace/bracket depth, string/escape-aware). If `IsJson` (JsonDocument.Parse) → structural Json. Else `failedAttempts++`.
   - Trimmed starts `<` (not `<!--`) → `FindXmlEnd` (self-closing `/>` or matching `</name`). If `IsXml` (XElement.Parse) → structural Xml. Else `failedAttempts++`.
3. Empty line → flush block. Other lines accumulate into unstructured block.
4. Flush at end, then `Merge`: adjacent non-structural spans with same type and whitespace-only gap merge.

**MaxFailedStructureAttempts = 32**: caps failed JSON/XML scans (avoids quadratic time on unbalanced input).

**Classify(text)** on non-blank lines (empty → Prose):
1. First line trimmed starts `$` → ShellTranscript
2. ≥2 lines match Log → Log
3. ≥2 lines match Search → SourceCode
4. ≥2 lines, ≥80% are Path lines containing `.` → DirectoryListing
5. ≥2 lines, ≥80% match Config → Toml
6. any Markdown line → Markdown
7. else Prose

**Regexes** (all Compiled, CultureInvariant):
- Log: `^\s*\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}[T ]\S+\s+(TRACE|DEBUG|INFO|WARN|WARNING|ERROR|FATAL)\b`
- Search: `^\S+:\d+`
- Path: `^\S+$`
- Config: `^\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.\-]*\s*=\s*.+$`
- Markdown: `^\s*(#{1,6}\s|[-*+]\s|\d+\.\s|>\s)`

# Research: reading/restoring system proxy after crash (issue #21, ai-proxy)
Date 2026-10-23. Q: how read per-user system proxy on macOS/Windows/Linux (direct or via .NET), and how existing tools recover it after SIGKILL. Direction chosen: option (c), marker file + clear proxy if previous run left it set.

## Findings
**F1 [MEASURED]** .NET caches one proxy object per process; env vars override OS. With no `*_proxy` vars: `HttpClient.DefaultProxy` = `System.Net.Http.MacProxy`. With `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9`: `HttpEnvironmentProxy`. `WebRequest.GetSystemWebProxy()` same instance both calls. So .NET can't report OS proxy when env proxy var set. Evidence: scratchpad `probe.cs`, `dotnet run probe.cs`, SDK 10.0.402, macOS 27.0.1; printed type, ReferenceEquals, GetProxy(https://api.anthropic.com/).

**F2 [READ]** `HttpClient.DefaultProxy` inits from `SystemProxyInfo.Proxy` (`Lazy<IWebProxy>`). `WebRequest.GetSystemWebProxy()` returns `DefaultProxy`. Each OS factory tries `HttpEnvironmentProxy` first. Evidence (dotnet/runtime main): `System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/HttpClient.cs` (~18, 39-45); `SocketsHttpHandler/SystemProxyInfo.cs:8-10`; `System.Net.Requests/src/System/Net/WebRequest.cs:548`; `SystemProxyInfo.OSX.cs`, `.Windows.cs`, `.Unix.cs`.

**F3 [READ]** Liveness of cached object by OS:
- macOS: `MacProxy` calls `CFNetworkCopySystemProxySettings` per `GetProxy`; live. (`SocketsHttpHandler/MacProxy.cs:84`)
- Windows: `HttpWindowsProxy` watches Internet Settings key via `RegNotifyChangeKeyValue`; reads via `WinHttpGetIEProxyConfigForCurrentUser`. (`HttpWindowsProxy.cs` ctor ~35-45; `WinInetProxyHelper.cs` ~28)
- Linux: env vars only, never gsettings/KDE, frozen at first use. (`SystemProxyInfo.Unix.cs`)
None exposes raw settings (host, port, enable flag); only resolves one URI at a time.

**F4 [MEASURED]** macOS per-network-service setting; read needs no privilege. On this Mac (27.0.1, standard user, no proxy): `scutil --proxy` showed merged global view (only `ExceptionsList`, `FTPPassive`); `networksetup -listallnetworkservices` listed 3 services; `-getwebproxy` and `-getsecurewebproxy Wi-Fi` both `Enabled: No`.

**F5 [READ]** `networksetup` writes need admin; `man networksetup`: "requires at least admin privileges to change network settings". Root if prefs locked.

**F6 [MEASURED]** Titanium.Web.Proxy 7.0.26 public: `SetAsSystemProxy`/`TrySetAsSystemProxy`, `DisableSystemProxy`/`TryDisableSystemProxy`, `DisableSystemHttp(s)Proxy`, `RestoreOriginalProxySettings`/`TryRestoreOriginalProxySettings`. No public read of current setting. Evidence: scratchpad `meta.cs` (System.Reflection.Metadata over `src/AiProxy/bin/Release/net10.0/Titanium.Web.Proxy.dll`, filter "Proxy").

**F7 [READ]** Titanium snapshot is in-memory only, all 3 backends; restores on ProcessExit/unhandled exception/signals: Windows `originalValues`; macOS `MacOsSystemProxyBackend._original`; Linux gsettings/KDE snapshots + `_originalEnv`. SIGKILL skips restores. No persisted snapshot found (keyword scan, not full read); no upstream issue on stale proxy after crash. **F8 [READ]** No .NET package offers cross-platform crash-safe system proxy handling. NuGet: Windows WinINet only: `Vanara.PInvoke.WinINet` 5.0.7 (~193k dl), `WinInetHelper`, `Riverside.Win32.Networking.Internet`. None persists state. **F9 [READ]** Charles: "doesn't have an opportunity to reset your proxy settings. It should notice that when it is restarted." Mechanism closed source. https://www.charlesproxy.com/documentation/faqs/can-no-longer-browse-without-charles-running/

**F10 [READ]** HTTP Toolkit never sets system proxy: launches preconfigured browsers, injects env vars into terminals. https://httptoolkit.com/docs/reference/intercept-page/

**F11 [INFERRED]** Detect crash from ai-proxy's own data (no OS read; original gone after SIGKILL anyway):
- Before `Set`, write marker under `~/.ai-proxy`.
- Hold open with `FileShare.None`; on Unix .NET uses `flock`, released by kernel on process death.
- Delete marker on clean restore.
- Next start: marker exists but unlocked → previous run died with proxy set. Locked → another instance live. Clear via `TryDisableSystemProxy` before Titanium snapshots.
`flock` behavior from memory; implementation test pending.

**F12 [INFERRED]** Option (a), full-fidelity restore, = 3 OS backends owned by ai-proxy:
- macOS: read/write every network service.
- Windows: write registry values and `DefaultConnectionSettings` blob, broadcast `INTERNET_OPTION_SETTINGS_CHANGED`.
- Linux: gsettings and KDE.
Titanium has this code privately; duplicating it is the cost of keeping a corporate proxy a crash overwrote.

**F13 [MEASURED]** Child reading pipe from parent gets EOF when parent SIGKILLed, no delay (1.00s = parent's sleep). Child then ppid 1 (launchd). **F14 [READ]** Titanium sets system proxy only for endpoint in same running `ProxyServer`. `TrySetAsSystemProxy` → `ValidateEndPointAsSystemProxy` throws "Cannot set endPoints not added to proxy as system proxy" unless `ProxyEndPoints.Contains(endPoint)` and `ProxyRunning`. Evidence: `ProxyServer.cs:1748-1756`, `ProxyServer.SystemProxy.cs:108-133` (v7.0.26).

**F15 [READ]** Titanium snapshots only as side effect of write; differs by OS. `TryDisableSystemProxy(protocol)` → backend `RemoveProxy`, snapshots first. With `ProxyProtocolType.None`:
- macOS: snapshots, writes nothing (writes guarded by protocol flag).
- Windows: rewrites `ProxyEnable=1` whenever `ProxyServer` has a value; turns on a proxy the user configured but disabled.
- Linux: disables GNOME, KDE, env vars regardless of protocol.
So side-effect-free snapshot via Titanium public API: macOS only. `TryDisableSystemProxy` needs no registered endpoint or running server, so sidecar can always clear. macOS backend also restores snapshot on `ProcessExit`/`UnhandledException`; writes via `networksetup` with elevation fallback. Evidence: `MacOsSystemProxyBackend.cs:30-38, 82-100, 220-234`; `SystemProxy.cs:189-219`; `LinuxSystemProxyBackend.cs:155-222`; `ProxyServer.SystemProxy.cs:276-292`.

**F16 [INFERRED]** Sidecar restores true original only if ai-proxy captures snapshot itself. Sidecar can't `Set`; on Windows/Linux can't snapshot via Titanium without changing settings; parent's private snapshot dies with it. Choice:
- Sidecar that clears via Titanium public API on all OSes.
- Sidecar restoring from ai-proxy's own snapshot: per-OS reads/writes = F4 (macOS), registry values (Windows), gsettings/KDE (Linux). Snapshot file in `~/.ai-proxy` can double as crash marker.

F11 [INFERRED] Crash detection needs no OS proxy API. From F3, F6: no portable read. From F7: original lost on SIGKILL. Detect from own data:

- Hold open with `FileShare.None` (Unix: .NET uses `flock`, kernel drops on death).

- Next start: marker exists, unlocked → previous run died with proxy set. Locked → another instance live.

F12 [INFERRED] Option (a), full-fidelity restore, means owning three OS backends:
- macOS: read/write every network service.
- Windows: registry values + `DefaultConnectionSettings` blob, broadcast `INTERNET_OPTION_SETTINGS_CHANGED`.
- Linux: gsettings and KDE.
Titanium has this privately. Duplicating it is the cost of keeping a corporate proxy a crash overwrote.

F13 [MEASURED] Child reading pipe from parent gets EOF the moment parent is SIGKILLed. Child in own session, blocked on stdin; read returned at 1.00s, matching parent sleep before SIGKILL; no detection delay; child reparented to launchd (ppid 1). Pipe EOF is a portable parent-died signal, no polling, immune to PID reuse. Evidence: scratchpad `parent.py`/`child.py` (Python 3.15, macOS 27.0.1); `Popen(stdin=PIPE, start_new_session=True)`; parent `os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGKILL)`, exit 137; child wrote `EOF after 1.00s, ppid now 1`. F14 [READ] Titanium sets system proxy only for an endpoint registered in the same running `ProxyServer`. `TrySetAsSystemProxy` → `ValidateEndPointAsSystemProxy` throws "Cannot set endPoints not added to proxy as system proxy" unless `ProxyEndPoints.Contains(endPoint)` and `ProxyRunning`. Evidence: titanium v7.0.26 `src/Titanium.Web.Proxy/ProxyServer.cs:1748-1756`, `ProxyServer.SystemProxy.cs:108-133`.

F15 [READ] Titanium backends snapshot only as side effect of write; differs by OS. `TryDisableSystemProxy(protocol)` calls backend `RemoveProxy`, which snapshots first. With `ProxyProtocolType.None`:
- macOS: snapshots, writes nothing (writes guarded by protocol flag).
- Windows: rewrites `ProxyEnable=1` whenever `ProxyServer` has a value, turning on a proxy the user disabled.
- Linux: disables GNOME, KDE, env vars regardless of protocol.
So side-effect-free snapshot via Titanium public API exists on macOS only. `TryDisableSystemProxy` needs no registered endpoint or running server, so a sidecar can always clear.
macOS backend also restores snapshot on `ProcessExit`, `UnhandledException`; writes via `networksetup` with elevation fallback.
Evidence: titanium v7.0.26 `Helpers/MacOsSystemProxyBackend.cs:30-38, 82-100, 220-234`, `Helpers/SystemProxy.cs:189-219`, `Helpers/LinuxSystemProxyBackend.cs:155-222`, `ProxyServer.SystemProxy.cs:276-292`.
